project.name: Online Food Delivery Platform
project.summary: A web service for customers to order food from restaurants, with admin and delivery partner interfaces.

functional_requirements: Customers can register and log in securely.
Customers can browse restaurants and view menus.
Customers can add items to a cart and place orders.
Customers can make online payments for orders.
Customers can track the delivery status of their orders.
non_functional_requirements: Authentication must follow industry‑standard security practices.
System response time shall be under 2 seconds for core operations.
Data storage must ensure high availability and durability.
Web interface must be responsive across desktop and mobile devices.

actors.name: Customer
actors.description: End user who orders food through the platform.

actors.name: Restaurant Administrator
actors.description: Manages restaurant profile, menus, and incoming orders.

actors.name: Delivery Partner
actors.description: Handles assigned deliveries and updates delivery status.

use_cases.name: Register and Login
use_cases.description: Customer creates an account and authenticates to access the platform.

use_cases.name: Browse Restaurants and Menus
use_cases.description: Customer searches for restaurants, views menus, and selects items.

use_cases.name: Place Order and Pay
use_cases.description: Customer adds items to cart, confirms order, and completes payment.

use_cases.name: Manage Restaurant Menu
use_cases.description: Administrator creates, updates, or removes menu items and restaurant details.

use_cases.name: Update Delivery Status
use_cases.description: Delivery partner marks deliveries as picked up, in‑transit, or delivered.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Customers can register and log in securely.
criteria: Email verification is required during registration.
Passwords must meet minimum complexity rules.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Customers can browse restaurants and view menus.
criteria: Restaurants can be filtered by cuisine and rating.
Menu items display name, description, price, and image.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Customers can add items to a cart and place orders.
criteria: Cart persists across sessions until checkout.
Order summary shows item details, quantities, and total price.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Customers can make online payments for orders.
criteria: System supports credit/debit card payments via a PCI‑compliant gateway.
Payment success or failure is communicated instantly to the user.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Customers can track the delivery status of their orders.
criteria: Real‑time status updates are shown on the order page.
Estimated arrival time is displayed and refreshed periodically.

user_stories.story: As a customer, I want to register and log in, so that I can securely access the platform.
acceptance_criteria: User can create an account with email and password.
User can log in using registered credentials and receive a session token.

user_stories.story: As a customer, I want to browse restaurants and view menus, so that I can choose what to order.
acceptance_criteria: Restaurants are listed with basic information and can be filtered by cuisine.
Selecting a restaurant displays its menu with item details and prices.

user_stories.story: As a customer, I want to add items to a cart and place an order, so that I can purchase food.
acceptance_criteria: Items can be added, updated, or removed from the cart before checkout.
Order submission creates an order record and triggers payment processing.

user_stories.story: As a customer, I want to make online payments, so that I can complete purchases securely.
acceptance_criteria: Supported payment methods include credit card and digital wallets.
Payment transaction returns success or failure status to the user.

user_stories.story: As a restaurant administrator, I want to manage menus and incoming orders, so that I can keep offerings up to date and fulfill orders.
acceptance_criteria: Admin can create, edit, or delete menu items and set availability.
Admin can view order details, update order status, and mark orders as ready.

user_stories.story: As a delivery partner, I want to view assigned deliveries and update delivery status, so that customers can track their orders.
acceptance_criteria: Delivery partner sees a list of assigned orders with pickup and drop-off addresses.
Partner can change status to 'Picked Up', 'In Transit', and 'Delivered', which updates the customer view.

UML Generator.use_case:
flowchart LR
    User -->|register/login| AuthSystem
    User -->|browse| WebApp
    User -->|place order| OrderSystem
    RestaurantAdmin -->|manage| AdminPortal
    DeliveryPartner -->|view/update| DeliveryPortal
    AuthSystem -->|authenticates| Database
    OrderSystem -->|processes| Database
    DeliveryPortal -->|updates status| Database
UML Generator.sequence:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant WA as WebApp
    participant AS as AuthService
    participant OS as OrderService
    participant DB as Database
    participant DP as DeliveryPartner
    U->>WA: login/register
    WA->>AS: authenticate
    AS->>DB: verify credentials
    DB-->>AS: result
    AS-->>WA: token
    U->>WA: browse restaurants/menu
    U->>WA: add items to cart
    U->>WA: place order
    WA->>OS: create order
    OS->>DB: store order
    DB-->>OS: orderId
    OS-->>WA: order confirmation
    OS->>DP: assign delivery
    DP->>OS: accept
    OS->>DP: delivery details
    DP->>OS: update status
    OS->>DB: update order status

Database Designer.sql:
CREATE TABLE Users (
    user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    name TEXT,
    email TEXT,
    password_hash TEXT,
    phone TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE Restaurants (
    restaurant_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    name TEXT,
    address TEXT,
    phone TEXT,
    admin_user_id INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (admin_user_id) REFERENCES Users(user_id)
);

CREATE TABLE MenuItems (
    item_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    restaurant_id INTEGER,
    name TEXT,
    description TEXT,
    price REAL,
    FOREIGN KEY (restaurant_id) REFERENCES Restaurants(restaurant_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Orders (
    order_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    user_id INTEGER,
    restaurant_id INTEGER,
    order_time DATETIME,
    status TEXT,
    total REAL,
    FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES Users(user_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (restaurant_id) REFERENCES Restaurants(restaurant_id)
);

}

    real price
}

    integer order_id PK
    integer user_id FK
    integer restaurant_id FK
    datetime order_time
    text status
    real total
}

Project Structure.architecture: A micro‑service style web app with a React/Vite SPA communicating over HTTPS to FastAPI services. FastAPI handles user, restaurant, order, and delivery domains, persisting data in PostgreSQL via SQLAlchemy. Redis provides session cache and async task queue (Celery) for payment processing and delivery notifications. Nginx terminates TLS and proxies to the API and static assets. Docker Compose orchestrates services for development and production.
Project Structure.architecture_diagram:
flowchart TD
    subgraph Client
        UI[React SPA]
    end
    subgraph API
        Auth[Auth Service]
        User[User Service]
        Restaurant[Restaurant Service]
        Order[Order Service]
        Delivery[Delivery Service]
    end
    subgraph Data
        DB[(PostgreSQL)]
        Cache[(Redis)]
    end
    UI -->|HTTPS| Auth
    UI -->|HTTPS| User
    UI -->|HTTPS| Restaurant
    UI -->|HTTPS| Order
    UI -->|HTTPS| Delivery
    Auth --> DB
    User --> DB
    Restaurant --> DB
    Order --> DB
    Delivery --> DB
    Order --> Cache
    Delivery --> Cache
    Cache -->|Pub/Sub| Delivery
    style Client fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style API fill:#bbf,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
    style Data fill:#bfb,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px

Documentation.readme: Online Food Delivery Platform enables users to register, browse restaurants, order meals, pay online, and track deliveries. Restaurants manage menus and orders; delivery partners handle assigned deliveries. Built with a responsive web UI, RESTful API, JWT authentication, and PostgreSQL storage.
Documentation.api_documentation: POST /auth/register – body {email,password,role}. POST /auth/login – returns JWT. GET /restaurants – list. GET /restaurants/{id}/menu – list items. POST /cart – add item. GET /cart – view. POST /orders – place order. GET /orders/{id} – status. PATCH /orders/{id}/status – delivery partner update. Admin endpoints: POST/PUT/DELETE /admin/restaurants, /admin/menu, /admin/items.
Documentation.installation: Clone repo, run `npm install` for server and client, set up PostgreSQL DB, configure .env with DB_URL and JWT_SECRET, run `npm run migrate` to create tables.
Documentation.deployment: Containerize with Docker, use docker-compose to launch app, db, and nginx. Deploy to cloud (AWS ECS/EKS or Azure AKS). Enable HTTPS via Let’s Encrypt. Scale horizontally with load balancer.
Documentation.sprint_plan: Sprint 1: Auth, user registration, login. Sprint 2: Restaurant listing, menu API. Sprint 3: Cart and order placement. Sprint 4: Payment integration, order tracking. Sprint 5: Admin UI for restaurant management. Sprint 6: Delivery partner UI, status updates. Sprint 7: Performance testing, security audit, CI/CD pipeline.
Documentation.architecture: Frontend: React SPA with Redux, responsive design. Backend: Node.js/Express REST API, JWT auth, service layer. Database: PostgreSQL with indexed tables for users, restaurants, items, orders. Deployment: Docker containers behind Nginx reverse proxy, load-balanced, stateless API servers, persistent DB volume.
